target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2023 disclosure covers the assumption of VMware equity awards for continuing employees and the acceleration/conversion of non-employee director awards. The 2024 filings split this topic: D071 covers the assumption/conversion of employee RSU/PSU awards (and director acceleration), while D126 specifically details the assumption of awards under the 2007 Plan and the conversion into 46 million Broadcom RSUs for continuing employees. These two 2024 disclosures collectively cover the subject matter of the single 2023 disclosure regarding equity award assumption.

comparisons.peer_topic: RSU and PSU Grant Terms and Vesting
comparisons.peer_summary: The 2006 Plan authorizes RSUs and stock options, with PSUs granted to senior officers and employees vesting after three years and one month. Other RSU and option awards generally vest over four years, with 10 million PSUs outstanding as of December 28, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose specific vesting schedules for their Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and Performance Stock Units (PSUs) under their respective equity plans. AVGO states that Broadcom RSUs assumed from the VMware Merger will vest generally over four years. Similarly, Intel discloses that 'Other RSU awards and option awards generally vest over four years from the grant date,' while its PSUs vest over a specific 'three years and one month' period. This establishes a direct comparability in how both companies structure the time-based and performance-based vesting timelines for their core equity awards.

PSUs vest three years and one month following the start of the performance period.
Other RSU awards and option awards generally vest over four years from the grant date.
